name: vscode-git-ignores-and-excludes
description: Keep your own notes and working files in the repo without committing them. Manage .git/info/exclude from the explorer, and see which rule ignores or excludes any file.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Runs git inside the workspace and writes to its .git/info/exclude file.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Needs a local file system and git on the PATH.

gitIgnoresAndExcludes.badges.enabled.markdownDescription: Show a badge in the File Explorer on ignored and excluded files, telling the three sources apart. Tooltips are shown either way. This covers the badge only: to mute a color, set it to whatever `gitDecoration.ignoredResourceForeground` resolves to in your theme under `workbench.colorCustomizations`.

configuration.title: Local Excludes

gitIgnoresAndExcludes.badges.localExclud.patternErrorMessage: A badge is at most two characters.
gitIgnoresAndExcludes.badges.localExclud.markdownDescription: Badge for files excluded by `.git/info/exclude`, which is never committed. Defaults to the fullwidth asterisk (U+FF0A), which fills the badge slot more evenly than an ASCII asterisk. One or two characters, or empty for no badge.

configuration.markdownDescription:
Files excluded by `.git/info/exclude`, which is never committed and nobody else sees.

They keep the color VS Code gives ignored files. To color them differently, set `gitIgnoresAndExcludes.localExcludesForeground` under `workbench.colorCustomizations`.

configuration.title: Global Excludes

gitIgnoresAndExcludes.badges.globalExclu.patternErrorMessage: A badge is at most two characters.
gitIgnoresAndExcludes.badges.globalExclu.markdownDescription: Badge for files excluded by the global excludes file (`core.excludesFile`), which applies to every repository. Empty by default, since a global rule is your own standing choice. One or two characters, or empty for no badge.

configuration.markdownDescription:
Files excluded by the file `core.excludesFile` names, which applies to every repository you clone.

They keep the color VS Code gives ignored files. To color them differently, set `gitIgnoresAndExcludes.globalExcludesForeground` under `workbench.colorCustomizations`.

configuration.title: Repository Ignores

gitIgnoresAndExcludes.badges.repositoryI.patternErrorMessage: A badge is at most two characters.
gitIgnoresAndExcludes.badges.repositoryI.markdownDescription: Badge for files ignored by a committed `.gitignore` at any depth. Empty by default, since a committed rule is shared and expected. One or two characters, or empty for no badge.

configuration.markdownDescription:
Files ignored by a committed `.gitignore`, so everyone on the team ignores them too.

They keep the color VS Code gives ignored files. To color them differently, set `gitIgnoresAndExcludes.repositoryIgnoresForeground` under `workbench.colorCustomizations`.

colors.description: Files excluded by .git/info/exclude (never committed). Defaults to the color VS Code already uses for ignored files.
Files excluded by the global excludes file (core.excludesFile). Defaults to the color VS Code already uses for ignored files.
Files ignored by a committed .gitignore. Defaults to the color VS Code already uses for ignored files.
